vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: macro-helper
Version: 1.0.2

The macro-helper skill is a legitimate utility designed to assist users with Excel VBA development. The bundle consists of a bash script (scripts/macro.sh) that acts as a template dispatcher, providing boilerplate VBA code, debugging checklists, and optimization tips via standard output. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection; the script performs no network or sensitive file system operations.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions match its stated purpose (VBA/macro generation, explanation, debugging, templates); it asks for no credentials, no installs, and the bundled script appears to only produce/format VBA examples — but you should review generated macros before running them because VBA can perform file and email actions.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (Macro Helper for Excel/VBA) aligns with the included files: SKILL.md documents the expected commands and the bundled scripts/macro.sh implements generate, explain, debug, template, convert and optimize. There are no unrelated binaries, cloud credentials, or surprising external services required.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent/user to run the included local script (bash scripts/macro.sh) and to paste VBA for explanation — the script emits VBA templates, explanations, and debugging guidance. It does not instruct reading unrelated system files or exfiltrating data. However, many of the generated VBA templates deliberately include file operations and Outlook automation (attachments, .Send) which are expected for this skill but are potentially impactful if run without review.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is present; this is instruction-only plus a bundled script. Nothing in the manifest downloads or executes remote code during install, which is low-risk for supply-chain or arbitrary-download concerns.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, credentials, or config paths are requested in the manifest. The skill's functionality (VBA generation and guidance) does not require additional secrets. The included VBA examples reference Outlook and file paths, which is appropriate for macros but does not imply the skill itself needs credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request persistent system privileges. It does not modify other skills or system-wide agent settings in the files provided.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally consistent for providing VBA/macro help: it contains a local shell script that prints and formats VBA code and guidance, asks for no secrets, and performs no network installs. Before installing or using it, review any VBA it generates before running in Excel — VBA can read/write files, control Outlook (send emails, attach workbooks), and delete or modify data. Specifically: 1) Inspect templates for .Send, file-delete, file-overwrite, or full-path operations and change .Send to .Display when testing; 2) Run generated macros in a disposable workbook or isolated environment; 3) If you need higher assurance, provide the full (untruncated) scripts/macro.sh content for review — the provided file in the prompt was truncated in the listing, so I lowered confidence accordingly; 4) If the skill points to an unknown homepage or contact, prefer cautious use and verify the publisher before running macros that interact with email or filesystem.
